title: Anisotropic domain wall velocity profiles in the creep regime: the interplay of chiral damping, stiffness and Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction
authors: Adriano Di Pietro, Alessandro Magni, Stefania Pizzini, Frowin Dörr, Yasser Shokr, Gianfranco Durin, Silvia Tacchi, Marco Madami, Giovanni Carlotti, Emily Darwin, Alexandra J. Huxtable, Christopher H. Marrows, Bryan J. Hickey, Michaela Kuepferling
abstract: The asymmetric expansion of magnetic bubble domains in ultrathin ferromagnets provides a powerful route to probe the interfacial Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI). While conventional analyses rely on domain wall velocities measured along selected directions as a function of in-plane field, recent approaches have highlighted the additional insight contained in the angular dependence of the velocity, $v(θ)$. Here, we develop an extended angular creep model that incorporates both the dispersive domain wall stiffness and a chirality-dependent prefactor associated with chiral damping. This generalization captures the full anisotropic dynamics of domain wall motion around a bubble domain. We show that these contributions significantly modify the angular velocity profile and can lead to features not accessible within existing models. Our results establish a more complete framework for interpreting creep-driven domain expansion and provide improved sensitivity for the quantitative extraction of DMI and chiral dynamical effects.
summary: This work develops an advanced theoretical model to analyze how domain wall velocity changes anisotropically during magnetic bubble expansion. By incorporating both dispersive stiffness and chiral damping into the creep model, the authors provide a more sensitive method for extracting fundamental parameters like the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya Interaction (DMI). The findings emphasize that accurate material characterization requires accounting for all physical contributions simultaneously.
main_problem: To develop a comprehensive framework for interpreting creep-driven domain expansion that accurately separates the contributions of chiral damping, dispersive domain wall stiffness, and Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction (DMI) to the anisotropic domain wall velocity profile v(theta).
main_result: The extended model successfully separates elastic/stiffness effects from dissipative (chiral damping) effects in the angular velocity profile, showing that rigorous DMI extraction requires accounting for both chiral damping and stiffness.
method: The authors developed an extended angular creep model incorporating dispersive domain wall stiffness and chirality-dependent prefactors to analyze measured full angular velocity profiles v(theta).
model_or_system: The study focuses on ultrathin ferromagnetic heterostructures with perpendicular magnetic anisotropy (PMA), analyzing asymmetric bubble expansion dynamics. The theoretical framework extends the standard creep model by adding terms for dispersive stiffness and chiral damping.
key_observables: Angular dependence of the domain wall velocity, v(theta); normalized angular velocity profile; separation into chiral damping term, prefactor, and creep exponential.
important_parameters: Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya Interaction (DMI) field (H_DMI), chiral damping coefficient ($\alpha_{CD}$), domain-wall stiffness ($	ilde{\sigma}$), and the creep exponent parameter ($\chi_0$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the bubble domain is large enough to ignore curvature-induced effects, and that independent measurements of DMI from flow regimes are available for comparison.
figures_summary: Figures show schematic setups for measuring v(theta) and plots comparing experimental angular velocity profiles against model predictions derived using energy-only vs. full models incorporating stiffness and chiral damping.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the need for an extended creep model to account for anisotropy in domain wall motion. It then details how this model separates contributions from various physical effects (stiffness, damping) by analyzing v(theta). Finally, it compares these findings with independent DMI estimates derived from flow-regime measurements.
why_interesting: While the primary focus is magnetism, the rigorous mathematical separation of multiple interacting energy/dissipation terms in a non-equilibrium system (creep dynamics) mirrors complex modeling challenges found in open quantum systems or driven many-body physics.
